correctness.rationale: Proof uses strict convexity of squared induced operator norm, first-order Hermitian eigenspace compression at the nilpotent endpoint, and the sine-spectrum of maximal-weight runs. Weighted-shift phase gauge and Perron variational principle give the exact other endpoint. Independent finite numerical checks are diagnostic only. Endpoint formulas checked analytically for every n and M>0; g strict convexity includes the equality boundaries, and monotonicity excludes t>1. The standalone numerical script passed representative reordering and nonuniform-weight cases.

originality.rationale: Semantic searches of published mathematical records of affine Jordan/nonnormal waveform/weighted shift variants and relevant primary literature found only an unweighted Jordan minimizer and a binary numerical-radius longest-run law. Their full statements were read and compared mathematically. Neither gives the sharp three-regime one-pass relaxation criterion for arbitrary nonbinary weights, particularly same-multiset order reversal. An unindexed older weighted-bidiagonal norm optimization remains a residual risk; search failure alone was not treated as proof.
residual_risks: Classical Birkhoff–James orthogonality and matrix nearness theory could contain a more general norm-minimizer criterion implying this family; no exhaustive historical index exists.
The companion arXiv:2606.29987 full manuscript was not materially inspected; its abstract does not justify whole-document absence of a covering result.
The theorem is a restricted one-lag model, not an exact reanalysis of the full multi-delay DNWR paper.

value.rationale: The optimization question arises naturally for finite-window, one-lag nonnormal relaxation, where spectral-radius minimization is always t=1 but one-sweep norm contraction may not agree. The complete classification for all finite dimensions and all nonbinary complex weights is structural, not an arbitrary parameter slice: exact contiguity of *maximum* edge weights decides endpoint optimality, and rearranging an unchanged weight multiset reverses the outcome. These conclusions inform choice of one-pass relaxation under variable temporal couplings.
